newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: EASTERN SAYS WANTS BIGGER PORTLAND SHARE.
newsitem.headline: EASTERN SAYS WANTS BIGGER PORTLAND SHARE.

text.p: Eastern Aluminium Ltd, which has a 10 percent interest in the Portland aluminium smelter in the Australian state of Victoria, was interested in acquiring the state government's 25 percent stake in the smelter, managing director Paul Exell said on Tuesday.

Addressing a base metals conference organised by broker Bell Securities, Exell said Eastern had a strongly positive long-term view of the aluminium industry and was keen to expand its asset base through attractive investments.
Targets were aluminium smelting, alumina refining and related bauxite mining, he said.
Other aluminium investments may be considered in special circumstances, he said.
Investments would preferably be in Australia though overseas opportunities may also be considered in due course, he said.
"The main present target is the (state) government's 25 percent interest in the Portland smelter, which is scheduled for privatisation," he said.
"Eastern Aluminium, along with its joint venture partners, have pre-emptive rights over this interest," he said.
Eastern did not intend becoming an operator in its own right, preferring to acquire minority positions in association with high calibre partners, he said.
The company had no debt and about A$16 million in cash, and this would be of considerable assistance in financing new investments, he said.
"However, investments will be typically large and financing will probably include new equity and debt raisings," he said.
Portland is owned 45 percent by Alcoa of Australia Ltd and 25 percent by the Victorian government through Aluminium Smelters of Victoria Pty Ltd (Aluvic).
The smelter produces about 294,000 tonnes of primary aluminium annually, mostly for sale in Victoria.
Other partners in the Portland smelter are Marubeni Corp with 10 percent and the Chinese state-owned China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) 10 percent.
Total capital expenditure at Portland so far was A$1.2 billion, Exell said.
Annual capital expenditure required to ensure the plant remained technologically up to date and to meet environmental, health and safety standards was about A$15 million a year, he said.
